meta.title: gRPC: The Contract, the Bytes, the Streams

hook.text: gRPC is not a magic speed switch.
hook.promise: See a shared contract become bytes and concurrent streams, then choose by tradeoff.

design.visualThesis: Follow a single typed message from a shared contract into binary bytes and independent streams; show constraints beside benefits.
design.motionGrammar: One message transforms across scenes; staggered reveals and intentional holds, no fake meters.
design.assetLanguage: Original vector diagrams; 1080x1920 design units scaled 2x by shared composition.

scenes.purpose: Contract, bytes, streams become the promise.
scenes.narration: gRPC is not a magic speed switch. Its real advantage is how services agree, exchange data, and stream.

motion.action: Three terms assemble into a connected system.
motion.settle: Contract, bytes, streams become the promise.

scenes.purpose: Two implementations share one typed interface.
scenes.narration: Start with a contract. A proto file defines methods and message types. Generate clients and server code from the same schema.

motion.action: A shared schema branches into client and server bindings.
motion.settle: Two implementations share one typed interface.

scenes.purpose: Nine UTF-8 bytes versus two binary bytes; body only.
scenes.narration: Then encode the message. In this tiny example, JSON takes nine bytes. Protocol Buffers takes two. That is the message body, not a speed benchmark.

motion.action: The literal JSON id 42 becomes the correct two-byte Protobuf encoding.
motion.settle: Nine UTF-8 bytes versus two binary bytes; body only.

scenes.purpose: HTTP/2 multiplexes; TCP loss can still block.
scenes.narration: HTTP/2 interleaves streams over one connection. But packet loss can still stall them at the TCP layer. REST can use HTTP/2 as well.

motion.action: Numbered colored frames interleave, pause together at loss, then resume.
motion.settle: HTTP/2 multiplexes; TCP loss can still block.

scenes.purpose: Two independent directions plus all four method labels.
scenes.narration: Calls can return one reply, or stream messages from either side. In a bidirectional call, both sides can keep sending independently.

motion.action: A single exchange becomes repeated messages in both directions.
motion.settle: Two independent directions plus all four method labels.

scenes.narration: Choose gRPC when shared contracts and streaming fit your services. Check browser requirements, and benchmark your workload. The right protocol is a tradeoff.

motion.action: Contracts and streaming connect to an explicit workload decision.

outro.takeaway: Contracts, compact messages, and streaming are useful; performance depends on the workload.
outro.cta: Check your clients and benchmark your workload.

revision.reason: User requested a complete quality remake; earlier autonomous editorial delegation applies.
